developments.title: GooeyPi Desktop Workspace Ported to Windows with AI Agent Features
detail: GooeyPi is a desktop workspace application for AI agents including Pi, OMP, and Prime Agent.
The application supports computer use, agentic browser functionality, realtime voice controls, and an automation desk.
The installer is available via GitHub, with a Windows Store version announced as forthcoming.
developments.why_it_matters: The GooeyPi Desktop Workspace provides users with a comprehensive platform for interacting with AI agents, enhancing their productivity and experience. The availability of the application on Windows expands its reach to a broader user base.

developments.title: Multi-Agent v2 Enables Delegation to Luna
detail: Multi-Agent v2 has shipped a new capability allowing its models to delegate tasks to any supported model, including Luna. The feature was announced by Eric Provencher, who confirmed it was released after extensive reliability testing.
Sol and Terra can now delegate to Luna, providing a free delegation path that helps users stay within usage limits while leveraging Luna’s capabilities.
developments.why_it_matters: The delegation support lets developers offload work to Luna, reducing token consumption and avoiding limits in multi‑agent workflows.

developments.title: Ahmad Reverse Engineers DSv4 Flash to Move Cat Feeders Off Cloud
detail: Ahmad reverse engineered DSv4 Flash to disclose leaked private keys.
The reverse engineering was done on the LAN with 48 UDP data points mapped.
The mapped data points include feed, laser, voice, and camera.
developments.why_it_matters: Ahmad's reverse engineering of DSv4 Flash allows for the automation of cat feeders without relying on the cloud, improving the security and autonomy of the system. This development has a concrete consequence of enhancing the operating-system security of the cat feeders.

developments.title: Multi-Agent v2 Gains Cross-Model Delegation to Luna and Other Supported Models
detail: A product called Multi-Agent v2 has shipped a new capability allowing its models to delegate tasks to any supported model, including Luna.
The feature was announced by eric provencher as having shipped recently after a development period to ensure reliability.
Tibo is promoting Sol as a fleet manager for Luna agents, suggesting these delegating models collaborate efficiently within the system.
developments.why_it_matters: Cross-model delegation enables specialized models to offload tasks to Luna or other models best suited for specific subtasks, potentially improving both capability and efficiency in multi-agent workflows. This shipped feature directly affects how AI agent systems can be orchestrated in production.

developments.title: Opus 4.6 Max Quality Runs on Single RTX 5090
detail: Opus 4.6 Max quality can be executed on a single RTX 5090 GPU, according to a recent post. The claim suggests that the model fits within the memory and compute limits of the RTX 5090, enabling high‑quality inference without needing larger hardware.
developments.why_it_matters: This allows users to run top‑tier AI inference on a consumer‑grade GPU, lowering cost and hardware barriers.

developments.title: DeepSeek v4 PRO 0813 Quant Released
detail: antirez uploaded the new Q2 quantized version (0813) of DeepSeek v4 PRO to HuggingFace.
The model file is available for download, though quality tests are still ongoing.
The release expands the range of quantized AI models for users seeking lower memory and compute requirements.
developments.why_it_matters: The quantized model allows developers to run DeepSeek v4 PRO with reduced resource usage, facilitating deployment on less powerful hardware.

developments.title: Rich Markdown Editor Adds Scoped Style Tag Rendering
detail: The markdown editor now honors <style> tags, rendering embedded widgets such as a mini calorie calculator directly within the document instead of as a raw HTML block.
Styles are scoped to prevent them from affecting the editor itself, and all tags are sanitized with JavaScript stripped, ensuring that rendered content cannot execute malicious code.
developments.why_it_matters: By safely rendering inline HTML styles, the editor enables richer markdown content while protecting users from XSS attacks, a concrete security improvement for developers embedding HTML in markdown.

developments.title: Sol-Advisor v2 Implements Risk-Based Lane Selection After Performance Failures
detail: Dan McAteer reports releasing version 2 of sol-advisor, an AI agent orchestration tool, after discovering the original design degraded performance. The initial version forced subagent lanes even when unnecessary, resulting in 86.7% pass@1 quality versus 93.3% for Sol alone, plus 7.05× higher token volume and 3.11× slower execution times.

The v2 release introduces a risk-level assessment system that evaluates task complexity before selecting an appropriate agent lane. This prevents unnecessary orchestration overhead by using simpler processing paths for straightforward tasks. McAteer reports initial results show significant improvements, though validation testing remains ongoing.
Users who have sol-advisor installed are advised to upgrade to the new version.
developments.why_it_matters: The v2 architecture directly addresses the efficiency and cost problems identified in testing, potentially reducing token consumption by over 7× for applicable tasks while improving output quality. This matters for teams running sol-advisor in production environments where compute costs and response latency directly impact operational budgets and user experience.

developments.title: Stripe Finalizing $7B+ OpenRouter Acquisition
detail: Bloomberg reports that Stripe has finalized an agreement to acquire OpenRouter for more than $7 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. OpenRouter is a startup that helps companies switch between artificial intelligence models. The deal represents a significant investment in AI infrastructure by a major payments company.
developments.why_it_matters: The acquisition places a key AI routing service under the control of a major payments company, potentially affecting how independent developers access and pay for AI model services. OpenRouter serves as a broker allowing users to route requests across multiple AI providers, making this a potential inflection point for AI access infrastructure.

developments.title: Codex 1M-Token Context Now Enabled for ChatGPT Accounts
detail: Codex now supports a 1M-token context window for GPT-5.6 Sol when accessed through ChatGPT accounts, in addition to API keys. Tibo confirms the feature was recently flipped on for ChatGPT usage. The configuration requires adding model = "gpt-5.6-sol", model_context_window = 1000000, and model_auto_compact_token_limit = 900000 to ~/.codex/config.toml, followed by restarting the Codex client.

Larger context windows allow Codex to retain more code, tool output, and conversation history before summarizing older material. The automatic compaction triggers around 900,000 tokens to leave headroom before hitting the limit. Single-session CLI overrides are also documented as an option without changing defaults.
Tibo notes the default context length was tuned carefully for performance and cost, implying the 1M setting may have tradeoffs despite being technically supported.
developments.why_it_matters: Users running Codex through ChatGPT accounts can now process significantly larger codebases and conversation histories in a single session, reducing the frequency of context resets and enabling longer continuous development workflows without switching to API-only access.

developments.title: Jeffrey Emanuel Releases Major Update to de-slopify Claude Code Skill
detail: Jeffrey Emanuel announced a major improvement to his /de-slopify skill, a Claude Code tool he has been using constantly for months. The skill takes AI-generated writing and automatically improves it to reduce the telltale signs of AI-generated "slop" in text such as READMEs, documentation, and marketing copy, according to the skill's documentation page.

Emanuel framed the update as a refinement rather than a replacement for human writing, noting that no substitute for human authorship exists yet. The improved skill is published at his skills.md site and is available for download.
developments.why_it_matters: The update targets a specific friction point in AI-assisted documentation workflows by offering an automated cleanup pass for AI-generated public-facing text, reducing the manual editing burden Emanuel himself reports encountering daily.

developments.title: Wright Flyer Web Simulation Added to FrankenSim with WebAssembly and ThreeJS
detail: Jeffrey Emanuel announced the creation of a physics‑based, parameterized Wright Flyer simulation that runs in real time within a web browser using WebAssembly and ThreeJS, integrated into the FrankenSim platform. The implementation was driven by the /planning‑workflow skill, which iteratively refined a markdown plan with GPT‑Pro before the code was written.

The simulation is publicly accessible via the provided link, offering an interactive demonstration of historical aircraft dynamics and serving as a showcase for high‑performance, browser‑based physics rendering.
developments.why_it_matters: The new simulation expands FrankenSim’s demo suite, providing a real‑time, browser‑based physics example that highlights WebAssembly’s capability to deliver high‑performance computation without requiring native installations.
